why: The uniform core cannot see or drive a direction, so the wall must carry it: a winner-take-all bump on the ring, released in bursts (B6's read-then-run, done by the ring). Between bursts the wall is held quiet and each node's state (tau 3) integrates its own light, a picture of the light around the body. R (clean switch, self 7) and its timer Q make a pacemaker gated by the dark detector D; each burst drives every wall node up (+6 from R), the brightest nodes cross first, their self- and neighbour-excitation (self 2, neighbours 1.5 each) recruits a small bump, and G (fast global inhibition on the uniform sum, -8) silences the rest. The bump's beats pull the cell toward its own side (alpha 0), toward the light. When R ends the burst, the bump decays (wall tau 3) before the next reading. S1-S3 adapt the wall as in fourier1 (uniform spokes, self 3.5, tau 100). D (near-critical on the uniform sum) keeps the cell quiet at night. Expected: bursts that pull toward brighter light in the mid field, nearly random in the far field, where the light across the body is ~30x below the sensors' noise.
